Simulate data with known calendar seasonality

simulate_BASTION_calendar.Rd

Generate observations, timestamps, and known components for calendar fitting examples.

Usage

simulate_BASTION_calendar(scenario = c("daily", "biweekly", "hourly"), seed = NULL)

Arguments

scenario

One of "daily", "biweekly", or "hourly"; default "daily".

seed

Optional nonnegative integer random seed.

Details

Each scenario generates y as the sum of its known components and independent zero-mean Gaussian noise. Timestamps use UTC.

"daily" generates daily observations from 2019 through 2021, including February 29, 2020. With t starting at zero, the trend is 50 + 0.005*t. Using midpoint calendar phases w within the week and a within the year, weekly seasonality is 3*cos(2*pi*w), and yearly seasonality is 8*sin(2*pi*a) + 2*cos(4*pi*a). Noise SD is 1.5.

"biweekly" generates 560 daily observations starting January 6, 2020. With t starting at zero, the trend is 100 + 0.01*t + 3*sin(2*pi*t/560), and seasonality is 6*sin(2*pi*t/14) + 2*cos(4*pi*t/14). Noise SD is 1.5.

"hourly" generates 2016 hourly observations starting January 1, 2024 (12 full weeks). With t starting at zero, the trend is 100 + 0.002*t. Using midpoint phase h within each day, daily seasonality is 10*sin(2*pi*h) + 2*cos(4*pi*h). Monday-to-Sunday effects are c(2, 3, 3, 2, 1, -5, -6), constant within each day. Noise SD is 2.

Value

A list with numeric observations y, POSIXct timestamps dates, a data frame truth containing the trend and seasonal components, the Gaussian noise vector, and its generating noise_sd.

See also

fit_BASTION_calendar
